jobDescription: A developer-tools company runs a large monorepo with several hundred engineers committing every day. The platform engineer maintains the CI build infrastructure and caching, builds internal command-line tools in Go, reports build times to engineering leadership, writes runbooks for tooling incidents and mentors engineers on the graduate programme through pairing and review. When CI slows down the whole company feels it, so the team publishes build health every week and keeps a runbook for each failure mode it has seen.
requirements: Maintains the CI build infrastructure and remote caching for a large monorepo.
Mentors graduate engineers through pairing and structured review.
Builds internal command-line tools in Go.
Measures and reports build times to engineering leadership.

evidence.text: Platform engineer at Vantor Labs (code-search software), January 2020 to present, maintaining the CI build infrastructure and remote cache for a monorepo of about four million lines.
Built a Go command-line tool that lets engineers reproduce CI failures locally with the same container image and environment variables as the pipeline.
Published a weekly build-time report (median and 90th-percentile CI duration, cache hit rate) to the engineering leadership channel.

Quarantined tests that failed intermittently three times in a week, filed tickets to the teams that own them and returned each test to the main suite once its owning team had fixed and re-run it twenty times without a failure.
Added a troubleshooting page for the remote cache to the team wiki, covering cache misses after base-image changes and how to clear a poisoned cache entry safely.

Work sample: the build-time report for one week in March 2024, with median and 90th-percentile CI durations by pipeline, the cache hit rate and the list of quarantined tests with their ticket numbers.

Written reference (former engineering manager, identity checked by the recruiter against the company directory): the candidate was the assigned mentor for three engineers in the 2023 graduate scheme, held weekly pairing sessions with each of them and signed off their on-call readiness checklists in October 2023.
Recruiter logistics note: the candidate can interview on Wednesdays, would start after a three-week notice period and has asked to meet the graduate programme coordinator during the onsite day.

propositions.text: The candidate mentored three engineers in the 2023 graduate scheme with weekly pairing sessions and signed off their on-call readiness checklists in October 2023.
propositions.rationale: The reference check records the former engineering manager's written confirmation of the assignment, the pairing and the sign-offs.

propositions.text: The candidate built a Go command-line tool that reproduces CI failures locally with the pipeline's container image and environment.
propositions.rationale: The resume entry describes the tool directly.

propositions.text: The candidate published a weekly build-time report with median and 90th-percentile CI durations and cache hit rate.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the report and the work sample shows one week of it.

gold.expectedGap: A remote-cache troubleshooting page is described, but no incident runbooks for developer tooling are documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the graduate-scheme mentoring record from the reference check as supported evidence, limited to the three engineers and 2023.
followUpTargets: Ask which developer-tooling incidents the candidate has written runbooks for and where they are kept.
